compensating.why: hop 1 collapses each pair of backslashes before the conversion
hop 4 doubles every backslash before the call
hop 3 drops a trailing backslash of the argument

ownership_reason: Only the gold sees each backslash together with the character before it, and the variant gold never appends a backslash, so no change of its input can put one into the result; hops 1 and 2 hold the whole string and the finished value, hops 3 and 4 pass the sequence and the builder along. The gold's javadoc promises the unescaped text of a backslash escaped character sequence, which for 'one \( \) \\' is 'one ( ) \'. The convention is pinned outside the gold: TokenQueue.chompBalanced takes the character after a backslash literally (last != ESC) and its javadoc leaves those escapes in its result and points to unescape for contains text; QueryParser.contains unescapes chompBalanced's output for :contains(text) (SelectorTest testPsuedoContainsWithParentheses selects 'This is bad)' with 'bad\)'); QueryParser.matches keeps the escapes for java.util.regex, where a doubled backslash is one literal backslash; TokenQueueTest chompEscapedBalanced asserts the unescaped form of an escaped argument. One-line edits above the gold that pass the suite either replace the gold's result with another implementation (a regular expression at any hop) or are fitted to the test input (a private-use placeholder at hop 1, which breaks hop 1's documented char-array conversion; a backslash appended at hop 2 when the sequence ends with two backslashes, which leaves 'a\\b' as 'ab').
